Then it ties all five moves into one agency-reporting strategy, ending with a clever free Monday report inside Webmaster Tools.
o1.biggest_mistake: The Lite usage-limit fix sits at #2 behind a report build that is still in beta, even though the data marks it as the fastest, cheapest money. The 'Here's the data' section is dense, which makes 'where we win' harder to scan.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Lead with the Lite top-up as the quickest win, and give 'where we win' its own short, scannable section.

o2.biggest_strength: The 'where we lose / where we don't / our biggest leak is not Semrush' structure is exactly what I asked for. It shows the working (27 × 89% × 54%) and adds the striking fact that only 37% of a Lite group survives 12 months.
o2.biggest_mistake: Move 1's '19% gain' assumes every agency trial won back from Semrush converts to paid. That is an optimistic projection that could inflate the bet. It also stamps an invented 'November 2026' date on the data, and move 5 (link-data content) is closer to the generic 'do more content' advice I didn't want.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the content move with something tied to the agency or Lite signals, make the move 1 projection realistic, and drop the made-up date.

reason: Both read my data correctly and avoid chasing PPC. The first gives me a sharper fifth move that builds on the agency-report bet and grounds its projections more carefully. The second is easier to scan but pads out to five with a generic content play and an inflated projection.
